title: Don’t Call It a Reset: The Modi-Xi Meeting Wasn’t a Turning Point
gist: The author argues Xi Jinping's September BRICS visit to New Delhi and meeting with Modi was not a turning point or reset in India-China relations, rejecting both the rapprochement and the India-US deterioration explanations. The excerpt is truncated.

insights.claim: Xi Jinping's September visit to New Delhi for the BRICS summit and his meeting with Modi did not mark a turning point or reset in India-China relations.
insights.speaker: Sana Hashmi
insights.so_what: Fade narratives of a durable India-China rapprochement when sizing geopolitical risk.

insights.claim: Both popular explanations for renewed India-China engagement, rapprochement and deteriorating India-US relations, overstate the shift in bilateral ties.
insights.speaker: Sana Hashmi
insights.so_what: Treat India-US strain as not automatically pushing India toward China.

insights.claim: Joint participation of India and China in BRICS and the SCO should not be mistaken for alignment of interests, since India's multilateralism is longstanding and China has not been a decisive factor in it.
insights.speaker: Sana Hashmi
insights.so_what: Multilateral membership is a weak signal of bilateral alignment.
